# Draft:Trivial Warfare

Trivial Warfare is an American trivia podcast created by Jonathan Oakes and Chris Hollister. The podcast is based in Jacksonville, Florida. It won the Podcast Awards in the Games & Hobbies category in 2017 and 2018, and Jonathan Oakes, Chris Hollister, Carmela Smith, and Ben Young were inducted into the Trivia Hall of Fame in 2019. The show was profiled by the Jacksonville Business Journal and received local media coverage on WJXT television and WJCT radio in 2019.
Hosts and contributors
The show has featured a rotating set of hosts and recurring contributors. The show's official About page lists hosts and contributors including Jonathan Oakes, Chris Hollister, Ben Young, Carmela Smith, Nick Groves, Zahkia Mendoza, Nikki Bates, Erin Barclay, and Robert Everett.
Format
Trivial Warfare is structured as a head-to-head trivia match. Episodes typically open with introductions and an unscored warm-up game called "Warm It Up Chris". This is followed by announcements and then the main game which is played over six rounds of three questions each. Questions are generally worth 10 points and the show includes a midpoint question between rounds three and four worth 20 points. The format also includes bonus scoring opportunities, including a once-per-game option for teams to predict an answer before the question is read (“Sherlocking”). The game concludes with “The Gauntlet,” a three-question wagering round in which teams wager any amount up to their accumulated points and win or lose the wager depending on whether they answer all three questions correctly. Episodes close with guest shout-outs and the chance to promote causes that they care about.
History
Jonathan Oakes created Trivial Warfare with Chris Hollister, and the show later expanded beyond the original pairing to include additional regular voices, including Carmela Smith and Ben Young. A 2019 profile in the Jacksonville Business Journal described the podcast as developing into a revenue-generating operation supported in part by listener funding and related activities and noted an online community including a Facebook group called the "Trivial Warfare Army" that had grown to more than 2,600 active members at the time. As of January 2026, the group’s public membership count was approximately 3,400.
Business model
In 2019, the Jacksonville Business Journal described the show's revenue strategy as including listener donations (including Patreon), advertising interest, merchandising, and paywalled distribution of portions of its catalog.
Podcasting educator Dave Jackson discussed Trivial Warfare as a case study in Patreon-based crowdfunding in his book Profit from Your Podcast, in Chapter 8 (“Crowdfunding”) under the section titled “Jonathan Oakes, Trivial Warfare: Real-Life Lessons from Patreon”.
Media coverage
WJCT's First Coast Connect featured Oakes in a 2019 segment that included a trivia matchup with station manager David Luckin. Trivial Warfare was also featured in a News4JAX (WJXT) television segment in which hosts Vic and Lauren participated in a trivia challenge; the segment was later published on YouTube.
Awards and recognition
Trivial Warfare won the People’s Choice Podcast Awards in the Games & Hobbies category in 2017 and 2018.
Jonathan Oakes, Chris Hollister, Carmela Smith, and Ben Young were inducted into the Trivia Hall of Fame in 2019.
